claim: Caenorhabditis elegans halts postembryonic growth and development shortly after hatching in response to monomethyl branched-chain fatty acid (mmBCFA) deficiency.
source_text: Caenorhabditis elegans halts postembryonic growth and development shortly after hatching in response to monomethyl branched-chain fatty acid (mmBCFA) deficiency.
evidence_reasoning: This is a well-established observation from prior work (cited in the manuscript) and confirmed by experimental data in this study.

claim: d17iso-glucosylceramide is a critical metabolite in regulating growth and development in C. elegans.
source_text: an mmBCFA-derived sphingolipid, d17iso-glucosylceramide, is a critical metabolite in regulating growth and development.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by genetic and biochemical experiments showing that disrupting d17iso-GlcCer biosynthesis causes developmental arrest and that this function is mediated through TORC1.

claim: The d17iso-glucosylceramide lipid function is mediated by TORC1 in the intestine.
source_text: this lipid function is mediated by TORC1 and antagonized by the NPRL-2/3 complex in the intestine.
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through genetic suppression experiments, RNAi knockdown, and tissue-specific rescue experiments showing intestinal TORC1 is required.

claim: The NPRL-2/3 complex antagonizes d17iso-glucosylceramide function in promoting postembryonic development.
source_text: this lipid function is mediated by TORC1 and antagonized by the NPRL-2/3 complex in the intestine.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by the finding that nprl-3(ku540) mutation suppresses mmBCFA deficiency-induced arrest and that NPRL-2/3 acts as a negative regulator of TORC1.

claim: The essential lipid function of d17iso-glucosylceramide is bypassed by activating TORC1.
source_text: Strikingly, the essential lipid function is bypassed by activating TORC1 or inhibiting NPRL-2/3.
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated experimentally by showing that TORC1-activating transgenes (raga-1Q63L, rheb-1Q71LQ72D, daf-15::rap-1(22)) suppress elo-5(-) L1 arrest.

claim: The essential lipid function of d17iso-glucosylceramide is bypassed by inhibiting NPRL-2/3.
source_text: Strikingly, the essential lipid function is bypassed by activating TORC1 or inhibiting NPRL-2/3.
evidence_reasoning: Shown by the nprl-3(ku540) mutation and nprl-2/3 RNAi experiments that suppress mmBCFA deficiency-induced developmental arrest.

claim: TOR complexes (TORC1 and TORC2) function in sensing various nutrient signals.
source_text: The target of rapamycin (TOR) complexes (TORC1 and TORC2) are known to function in sensing various nutrient signals
evidence_reasoning: This is established scientific knowledge cited from multiple references (Ma and Blenis, 2009; Laplante and Sabatini, 2012; Zoncu et al., 2012).

claim: TOR complexes are connected to growth, metabolism, stress responses, and cancers.
source_text: their roles are connected to growth, metabolism, stress responses, and cancers
evidence_reasoning: Established from prior literature cited in the manuscript (Hansen et al., 2008; He and Klionsky, 2009; Howell and Manning, 2011).

claim: Amino acids, energy, and growth factors have been described as nutrient inputs to TOR complexes.
source_text: While amino acids, energy, and growth factors have been described as nutrient inputs to TOR complexes
evidence_reasoning: This represents established knowledge from the TOR signaling field, referenced in the manuscript.

claim: Roles of lipid molecules as signals to TOR systems in controlling postembryonic growth and development were not known prior to this study.
source_text: roles of lipid molecules as signals to these systems in controlling postembryonic growth and development were not known.
evidence_reasoning: This is an assertion about the state of knowledge in the field prior to the current study, based on literature review.

claim: C. elegans enters L1 diapause when hatched in food-free surroundings.
source_text: When hatched in food-free surroundings, this nematode enters a quiescent state, termed L1 diapause
evidence_reasoning: This is well-established knowledge about C. elegans biology, cited from multiple references (Johnson et al., 1984; Munoz and Riddle, 2003; Baugh and Sternberg, 2006).

claim: An insulin/IGF-1 receptor signaling (IIS) pathway plays a critical role in the induction of L1 diapause and survival of developmentally arrested animals.
source_text: An insulin/IGF-1 receptor signaling (IIS) pathway plays a critical role in the induction of L1 diapause and survival of the developmentally arrested animals
evidence_reasoning: Established from prior studies cited in the manuscript (Gems et al., 1998; Baugh and Sternberg, 2006; Kniazeva et al., 2008; Lee and Ashrafi, 2008; Jones et al., 2009; Soukas et al., 2009).

claim: TOR complexes play prominent roles in regulating postembryonic growth and lifespan in C. elegans.
source_text: TOR complexes have also been indicated to play prominent roles in regulating postembryonic growth and lifespan in C. elegans
evidence_reasoning: Based on prior literature cited (Vellai et al., 2003; Syntichaki et al., 2007; Hansen et al., 2008; Honjoh et al., 2009; Lucanic et al., 2011).

claim: Monomethyl branched-chain fatty acids (mmBCFAs) are widely present in bacteria, plants, and animals, including humans.
source_text: Monomethyl branched-chain fatty acids (mmBCFAs) are widely present in bacteria, plants, and animals, including humans
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge from prior studies (Nicolaides and Ray, 1965; Ran-Ressler et al., 2008).

claim: In mammals, mmBCFAs are derived from branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs).
source_text: In mammals, mmBCFAs are derived from branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs)
evidence_reasoning: Established from prior research cited (Morii and Kaneda, 1982; Oku et al., 1994).

claim: The remainder of the de novo mmBCFA biosynthesis pathway in mammals has not been delineated.
source_text: although the remainder of the de novo pathway has not been delineated.
evidence_reasoning: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field regarding mammalian mmBCFA biosynthesis.

claim: The physiological roles of mmBCFAs are essentially unknown.
source_text: The physiological roles of these FA variants are essentially unknown
evidence_reasoning: This represents the state of knowledge in the field prior to this study, despite mmBCFAs being found at high levels in certain tissues.

claim: In C. elegans, mmBCFAs C15ISO and C17ISO are synthesized from the branched-chain amino acid leucine.
source_text: In C. elegans, readily detectable mmBCFAs C15ISO and C17ISO are synthesized from the BCAA leucine
evidence_reasoning: This was established in prior work by the authors (Kniazeva et al., 2004).

claim: The key enzymes in mmBCFA de novo synthesis pathway in C. elegans, including BCKDC, ELO-5, and ACS-1, are evolutionarily conserved.
source_text: The key enzymes in this de novo synthesis pathway, including the branched-chain ketoacid dehydrogenase complex (BCKDC), an FA elongase (ELO-5), and an acyl CoA synthetase (ACS-1), are evolutionarily conserved
evidence_reasoning: Based on prior work by the authors (Kniazeva et al., 2004, 2008) showing conservation of these enzymes.

claim: Newly hatched C. elegans that are deficient for mmBCFAs cannot initiate postembryonic growth and development, and instead enter L1 diapause.
source_text: newly hatched C. elegans that are deficient for mmBCFAs cannot initiate postembryonic growth and development, and instead enter L1 diapause.
evidence_reasoning: This was previously shown by the authors (Kniazeva et al., 2004, 2008) and is confirmed in the current study.

claim: The developmental arrest caused by mmBCFA deficiency is independent of the IIS pathway.
source_text: Further genetic analysis suggested that this developmental arrest is independent of the IIS pathway
evidence_reasoning: Based on genetic analysis from prior work (Kniazeva et al., 2004, 2008).

claim: elo-5 loss-of-function mutants are deficient for mmBCFAs and are developmentally arrested at the early L1 stage.
source_text: elo-5 loss-of-function mutants (termed elo-5(−) hereafter) are deficient for mmBCFAs and are developmentally arrested at the early L1 stage.
evidence_reasoning: This phenotype is demonstrated experimentally in this study and was previously reported (Kniazeva et al., 2004, 2008).

claim: The elo-5(-) developmental arrest phenotype is completely rescued by dietary supplementation of mmBCFAs.
source_text: This phenotype is completely rescued by dietary supplementation of mmBCFAs
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated experimentally in prior work (Kniazeva et al., 2004, 2008) and confirmed in this study.

claim: In mmBCFA-deficient elo-5(-) larvae, the amount of mmBCFA-containing sphingolipids are dramatically reduced.
source_text: We found that in mmBCFA-deficient elo-5(−) larvae, the amount of mmBCFA-containing sphingolipids were dramatically reduced
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct observation from mass spectrometry analysis performed in this study.

claim: Sphingolipids are a class of well-known bioactive lipids.
source_text: Sphingolipids are a class of well-known bioactive lipids
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge in the field of lipid biology.

claim: d17iso-sphinganine (d17iso-SPA) purified from S. spiritivorum is sufficient to overcome elo-5(-) L1 arrest.
source_text: This purified d17iso-SPA fraction, but not a chemically synthesized c17iso-sphingolipid with a straight-chain d18:1-LCB or a straight-chain LCB d16-SPA, was found to be sufficient to overcome elo-5(−) L1 arrest
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through dietary supplementation experiments showing rescue of developmental arrest.

claim: Straight-chain sphingolipids (c17iso with d18:1-LCB or d16-SPA) cannot rescue elo-5(-) L1 arrest.
source_text: This purified d17iso-SPA fraction, but not a chemically synthesized c17iso-sphingolipid with a straight-chain d18:1-LCB or a straight-chain LCB d16-SPA, was found to be sufficient to overcome elo-5(−) L1 arrest
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through dietary supplementation experiments showing lack of rescue.

claim: Custom synthesized d17iso-SPA efficiently rescues elo-5(-) developmental arrest.
source_text: Additionally, efficient rescue was also achieved with a custom synthesized d17iso-SPA
evidence_reasoning: Shown experimentally through supplementation assays (Figure 1D).

claim: d17iso-sphingolipid is sufficient to promote the postembryonic growth and development of mmBCFA-deficient animals.
source_text: Therefore, d17iso-sphingolipid is sufficient to promote the postembryonic growth and development of mmBCFA-deficient animals.
evidence_reasoning: Concluded from the rescue experiments showing d17iso-SPA supplementation overcomes elo-5(-) arrest.

claim: d17iso-SPA suppresses L1 arrest at a much lower concentration than C15ISO or C17ISO.
source_text: We observed that d17iso-SPA suppressed the L1 arrest at a much lower concentration than C15ISO or C17ISO
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through dose-response experiments (Figure 1D).

claim: Low concentrations of d17iso-SPA suppress L1 arrest without restoring mmBCFA levels.
source_text: we observed that the low concentrations of d17iso-SPA suppressed the L1 arrest without restoring mmBCFA levels
evidence_reasoning: Shown by gas chromatography analysis (Figure 1E) combined with rescue assays.

claim: Supplementation with d17iso-SPA, but not mmBCFAs, suppresses the L1 arrest phenotype caused by sptl-1 RNAi.
source_text: we found that supplementation with d17iso-SPA, but not mmBCFAs, also suppressed the L1 arrest phenotype caused by feeding RNAi of sptl-1
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated experimentally through RNAi and supplementation assays (Figure 1B).

claim: sptl-1 encodes a serine palmitoyltransferase homolog in C. elegans required for d17iso-SPA biosynthesis.
source_text: sptl-1, a gene encoding a serine palmitoyltransferase homolog in C. elegans required for d17iso-SPA biosynthesis
evidence_reasoning: Based on prior characterization of sptl-1 (Seamen et al., 2009).

claim: mmBCFAs promote postembryonic development through d17iso-SPA.
source_text: We thus conclude that mmBCFAs promote postembryonic development through d17iso-SPA.
evidence_reasoning: Concluded from multiple lines of evidence including rescue experiments, dose-response studies, and genetic analysis.

claim: fath-1 encodes a homolog of mammalian fatty acid 2-hydrolase (FA2H) responsible for the synthesis of the FA side chain of ceramides.
source_text: fath-1(C25A1.5) encodes a homolog of mammalian fatty acid 2-hydrolase (FA2H) responsible for the synthesis of the FA side chain of ceramides
evidence_reasoning: Based on sequence homology and functional characterization.

claim: cgt-1 and cgt-3 encode two ceramide glucosyltransferases that glucosylate ceramides to GlcCer.
source_text: cgt-1 and cgt-3 encode two ceramide glucosyltransferases that glucosylate ceramides to GlcCer
evidence_reasoning: Based on functional characterization of these genes.

claim: fath-1(RNAi)-treated animals cause larval arrest.
source_text: Both fath-1(RNAi)-treated animals (Figure 1B; Supplementary file 1) and the cgt-1(−);cgt-3(−) double mutant (Marza et al., 2009) cause larval arrest.
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated experimentally through RNAi experiments (Figure 1B).

claim: The cgt-1(-);cgt-3(-) double mutant causes larval arrest.
source_text: Both fath-1(RNAi)-treated animals (Figure 1B; Supplementary file 1) and the cgt-1(−);cgt-3(−) double mutant (Marza et al., 2009) cause larval arrest.
evidence_reasoning: Shown in this study and previously reported (Marza et al., 2009).

claim: The arrest caused by fath-1(RNAi) or cgt-1(-);cgt-3(-) double mutant could not be overcome by feeding d17iso-SPA.
source_text: We found the arrest under either condition could not be overcome by feeding d17iso-SPA
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through supplementation experiments (Figure 1B).

claim: Disrupting the function of glycosyltransferases that further modify GlcCer does not cause larval arrest.
source_text: Disrupting the function of glycosyltransferases that further modify GlcCer does not cause larval arrest
evidence_reasoning: Based on prior work (Griffitts et al., 2003).

claim: d17iso-glucosylceramide (d17iso-GlcCer) may be the lipid molecule that mediates the role of mmBCFAs and d17iso-SPA in promoting postembryonic growth and development in C. elegans.
source_text: These results suggest that d17iso-glucosylceramide (d17iso-GlcCer) (Figure 1A) may be the lipid molecule that mediates the role of mmBCFAs and d17iso-SPA in promoting postembryonic growth and development in C. elegans.
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from the genetic pathway analysis showing that enzymes downstream of d17iso-SPA but upstream of more complex sphingolipids are required.

claim: The ku540 mutation permits mmBCFA-depleted C. elegans to bypass L1 arrest and propagate continuously.
source_text: Mutation ku540 permits mmBCFA-depleted C. elegans to bypass L1 arrest and propagate continuously
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through genetic screening and phenotypic analysis (Figure 2).

claim: elo-5(-);ku540 mutant animals reach adulthood without C17ISO supplement.
source_text: elo-5(−);ku540 mutant animals reach adulthood without C17ISO supplement.
evidence_reasoning: Shown experimentally through growth assays (Figure 2B, 2C).

claim: elo-5(-);ku540 animals have no detectable C15ISO-containing or C17ISO-containing lipids.
source_text: elo-5(−);ku540 did not restore mmBCFA levels, and consequently the levels of d17iso-sphingolipids... elo-5(−);ku540 animals had no detectable C15ISO-containing or C17ISO-containing lipids
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through mass spectrometry and gas chromatography analysis (Figure 2D-G).

claim: elo-5(-);ku540 animals have ceramides and glucosylceramides containing straight chain d16LCB rather than d17isoLCB.
source_text: elo-5(-);ku540 animals had ceramides and glucosylceramides containing straight chain d16LCB rather than d17isoLCB
evidence_reasoning: Shown by mass spectrometry analysis (Figure 2F, 2G).

claim: The suppression of L1 arrest by the ku540 mutation is neither due to a change in mmBCFA nor the metabolism of the derived sphingolipids.
source_text: These data indicated that the suppression of L1 arrest by the ku540 mutation is neither due to a change in mmBCFA nor the metabolism of the derived sphingolipids.
evidence_reasoning: Concluded from lipid analysis showing no restoration of mmBCFAs or d17iso-sphingolipids in elo-5(-);ku540 animals.

claim: ku540 renders mmBCFAs nonessential for C. elegans development.
source_text: Therefore, our data suggest that ku540 renders mmBCFAs nonessential for C. elegans development.
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from the observation that elo-5(-);ku540 animals develop normally without mmBCFAs.

claim: ku540 suppresses the L1 arrest caused by RNAi of fath-1.
source_text: We found that the L1 arrest under both conditions, just like the arrest caused by elo-5(−), was effectively suppressed by ku540
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated experimentally (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).

claim: ku540 suppresses the L1 arrest caused by mutating both cgt-1 and cgt-3.
source_text: We found that the L1 arrest under both conditions, just like the arrest caused by elo-5(−), was effectively suppressed by ku540
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated experimentally (Figure 2H, 2I).

claim: d17iso-GlcCer mediates the roles of mmBCFAs and d17iso-SPA in postembryonic development.
source_text: These results provided strong evidence that d17iso-GlcCer mediated the roles of mmBCFAs and d17iso-SPA in postembryonic development.
evidence_reasoning: Concluded from genetic epistasis experiments showing ku540 suppresses defects in the GlcCer biosynthesis pathway.

claim: ku540 bypasses the requirement of mmBCFAs and d17iso-GlcCer in development by modifying a regulatory function downstream of d17iso-GlcCer.
source_text: our biochemical and genetic data indicate that ku540 bypasses the requirement of mmBCFAs and d17iso-GlcCer in development and does so by modifying a regulatory function downstream of d17iso-GlcCer.
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from the combination of lipid analysis and genetic suppression data.

claim: ku540 is a loss-of-function missense mutation of nprl-3.
source_text: ku540 is a loss-of-function mutation of nprl-3 that may function with nprl-2
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through genetic mapping, sequencing, and complementation analysis (Figure 3).

claim: The ku540 mutation changes a conserved glycine residue (G388) to glutamic acid in NPRL-3.
source_text: The ku540 mutation changes a conserved glycine residue (G388) to glutamic acid
evidence_reasoning: Determined through DNA sequencing (Figure 3A, 3B).

claim: NPRL-3 is conserved in all eukaryotes.
source_text: NPRL-3 is conserved in all eukaryotes
evidence_reasoning: Based on sequence homology analysis across species (Figure 3B).

claim: nprl-3(RNAi) mimics the effect of the ku540 mutation in rescuing the L1 arrest phenotype caused by blocking mmBCFA or glucosyl-ceramide biosynthesis.
source_text: nprl-3(RNAi) mimics the effect of the ku540 mutation in rescuing the L1 arrest phenotype caused by blocking mmBCFA or glucosyl-ceramide biosynthesis.
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through RNAi experiments (Figure 3C).

claim: nprl-2 dsRNA injection rescues elo-5(-) animals from L1 arrest.
source_text: nprl-2 dsRNA injection also rescued 42.4% of elo-5(−) animals to or beyond L3 stage
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through injection RNAi experiments (Figure 3C).

claim: NPRL-2 and NPRL-3 in C. elegans may function in a complex to negatively impact mmBCFA/d17iso-GlcCer-mediated L1 growth.
source_text: This suggested that NPRL-2 and NPRL-3 in C. elegans may also function in a complex to negatively impact mmBCFA/d17iso-GlcCer-mediated L1 growth.
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from the observation that RNAi of either nprl-2 or nprl-3 suppresses elo-5(-) arrest, similar to yeast NPR2/3.

claim: In S. cerevisiae, NPR3 forms a heterodimer with NPR2.
source_text: In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, NPR3 was shown to form a heterodimer with NPR2.
evidence_reasoning: Based on prior work in yeast (Neklesa and Davis, 2009).

claim: Mutations in both NPR2 and NPR3 in S. cerevisiae cause multiple growth defects when cells are cultured in low-quality amino acid conditions.
source_text: Mutations in both proteins cause multiple growth defects when cells were cultured in low-quality amino acid conditions
evidence_reasoning: Based on prior work in yeast (Neklesa and Davis, 2009).

claim: The NPR2/3 complex was proposed to be a negative regulator of the TOR pathway in S. cerevisiae.
source_text: The NPR2/3 complex was proposed to be a negative regulator of the TOR pathway in S. cerevisiae
evidence_reasoning: Based on prior work showing that blocking TOR suppresses NPR2/3 mutant defects (Neklesa and Davis, 2009).

claim: Reducing, but not eliminating, TORC1 activity reverses the rescue effects of nprl-3(ku540) on elo-5(-) mutant background.
source_text: then reducing, but not eliminating, TORC1 activity may reverse the rescue effects of nprl-3(ku540) on elo-5(−) mutant background.
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through RNAi experiments targeting TORC1 components (Table 1).

claim: C. elegans has orthologs of key components of mammalian TORC1, including raga-1 (RagA) and rheb-1 (Rheb).
source_text: Caenorhabditis elegans has orthologs of key components of mammalian TORC1, including regulatory elements raga-1 (RagA) and rheb-1 (Rheb)
evidence_reasoning: Based on sequence homology and prior characterization (Long et al., 2002; Schreiber et al., 2010).

claim: Feeding RNAi of raga-1 and rheb-1 are specific and effective to reduce, but not eliminate, TORC1 function.
source_text: Feeding RNAi of raga-1 and rheb-1 have been shown to be specific and effective to reduce, but not eliminate, TORC1 function
evidence_reasoning: Based on prior studies (Hansen et al., 2007; Syntichaki et al., 2007; Lemire et al., 2009).

claim: The suppression of elo-5(-) L1 arrest by nprl-3(ku540) dramatically decreases when raga-1(RNAi) or rheb-1(RNAi) are applied.
source_text: While nprl-3(ku540) effectively suppressed the L1 arrest phenotype of elo-5(−), the suppression dramatically decreased when raga-1(RNAi) or rheb-1(RNAi) were applied to the elo-5(−) nprl-3(ku540) double mutant
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated experimentally through RNAi experiments (Table 1).

claim: The rescue effect of nprl-3(ku540) on elo-5(-) depends on intact TORC1 activity.
source_text: This indicates that the rescue effect of nprl-3(ku540) on elo-5(−) depends on intact TORC1 activity.
evidence_reasoning: Concluded from the observation that reducing TORC1 activity reverses the ku540 suppression effect.

claim: The effects of raga-1(RNAi) and rheb-1(RNAi) in reversing nprl-3(ku540) suppression are eliminated by C17ISO supplementation.
source_text: We found that the effects of raga-1(RNAi) and rheb-1(RNAi) in the above tests were essentially eliminated by C17ISO supplementation
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated experimentally (Table 1).

claim: Reducing TORC1 activity neutralizes the effect of nprl-3(ku540) and restores the L1 arrest phenotype of elo-5(-).
source_text: In other words, reducing, but not eliminating, TORC1 activity neutralized the effect of nprl-3(ku540) and restored the L1 arrest phenotype of elo-5(−).
evidence_reasoning: Concluded from RNAi experiments showing that partial TORC1 knockdown reverses ku540 suppression in the absence of C17ISO.

claim: elf4E (ife-2) and p70S6K (rsks-1) are well-known downstream targets of TORC1 in C. elegans.
source_text: C. elegans orthologs of elf4E (ife-2) and p70S6K(rsks-1), two well-known downstream targets of TORC1
evidence_reasoning: Based on prior characterization of the TORC1 pathway (Long et al., 2002; Syntichaki et al., 2007; Anjum and Blenis, 2008; Sheaffer et al., 2008).

claim: elo-5(-) nprl-3(ku540) animals treated with ife-2(RNAi) or rsks-1(RNAi) yield results similar to those obtained with raga-1(RNAi) and rheb-1(RNAi).
source_text: We found that elo-5(−) nprl-3(ku540) animals treated with ife-2(RNAi) or rsks-1(RNAi), with or without C17ISO supplement, yielded results similar to those obtained with raga-1(RNAi) and rheb-1(RNAi)
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated experimentally (Table 1).

claim: TORC1 acts downstream of d17iso-GlcCer and is negatively regulated by NPRL-3.
source_text: these results indicate that TORC1 acts downstream of d17iso-GlcCer and is negatively regulated by NPRL-3.
evidence_reasoning: Concluded from genetic epistasis experiments showing that TORC1 activity is required for nprl-3(ku540) suppression.

claim: let-363/TOR(-) mutations cause late larval arrest and other severe defects.
source_text: The let-363/TOR(−) mutations cause late larval arrest and other severe defects
evidence_reasoning: Based on prior characterization (Long et al., 2002).

claim: Injection RNAi of let-363/TOR causes an early embryonic lethal phenotype.
source_text: but injection RNAi causes an early embryonic lethal phenotype
evidence_reasoning: Based on prior work (Sonnichsen et al., 2005).

claim: LET-363/TOR plays critical regulatory roles in a broad range of developmental stages.
source_text: indicating that LET-363/TOR, a key component of both TORC1 and TORC2, plays critical regulatory roles in a broad range of developmental stages
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from the different phenotypes at different developmental stages when TOR is disrupted.

claim: A maternal effect largely masks LET-363/TOR roles in earlier developmental stages, including L1 growth.
source_text: a maternal effect largely masks its roles in earlier stages, including its likely functions during L1 growth.
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from the difference between injection RNAi (early lethal) and feeding RNAi or mutation (later defects).

claim: elo-5(-) nprl-3(-);let-363(RNAi) animals display pleiotropic phenotypes that cannot be rescued by C17ISO supplement.
source_text: elo-5(−) nprl-3(−);let-363(RNAi) animals displayed pleiotropic phenotypes that could not be rescued by C17ISO supplement
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated experimentally (Table 1).

claim: The pleiotropic phenotypes of elo-5(-) nprl-3(-);let-363(RNAi) are consistent with TORC1 acting downstream of ELO-5.
source_text: which is consistent with TORC1 acting downstream of ELO-5.
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from the genetic epistasis relationship where complete loss of TORC1 cannot be rescued by mmBCFAs.

claim: Constitutive activation of TORC1 is sufficient to overcome the L1 arrest of elo-5(-) animals.
source_text: If d17iso-GlcCer mainly acts through TORC1 for the growth regulation function, constitutive activation of TORC1 should be sufficient to overcome the L1 arrest of elo-5(-) animals.
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through experiments with TORC1-activating transgenes (Figure 4).

claim: The daf-15::rap-1(22) transgene permits 50.6% of elo-5(-) animals to bypass L1 arrest and reach L3-adult stages.
source_text: We found that 50.6% of elo-5(−) animals containing the daf-15::rap-1(22) transgene bypassed L1 arrest and reached L3–adult stages
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated experimentally (Figure 4B).

claim: The raga-1Q63L transgene permits 50.4% of elo-5(-) mutants to bypass L1 arrest and reach L3-L4 stage.
source_text: We found that 50.4% of elo-5(−) mutants containing the raga-1Q63L transgene bypassed L1 arrest and reached L3–L4 stage
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated experimentally (Figure 4A).

claim: raga-1Q63L has been proven to constitutively activate TORC1 both in mammals and C. elegans.
source_text: raga-1Q63L that has been proven to constitutively activate TORC1 both in mammals and C. elegans
evidence_reasoning: Based on prior work (Kim et al., 2008; Schreiber et al., 2010).

claim: The rheb-1Q71LQ72D transgene permits 41.4% of elo-5(-) animals to grow beyond the L1 stage.
source_text: we also tested a third TORC1-activating transgene, rheb-1Q71LQ72D, and found that it also permitted 41.4% of elo-5(−) animals to grow beyond the L1 stage
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated experimentally (Figure 4A).

claim: TORC1 acts downstream of d17iso-GlcCer to promote L1 growth and development.
source_text: These results led to the conclusion that TORC1 acts downstream of d17iso-GlcCer to promote L1 growth and development
evidence_reasoning: Concluded from multiple lines of genetic evidence including TORC1 activation bypassing lipid deficiency.

claim: TORC1 activity in promoting L1 growth is negatively regulated by NPRL-2/3.
source_text: TORC1 acts downstream of d17iso-GlcCer to promote L1 growth and development and that this activity is negatively regulated by NPRL-2/3.
evidence_reasoning: Concluded from genetic epistasis experiments showing NPRL-2/3 loss-of-function activates TORC1-dependent growth.

claim: Biosynthesis and localization of mmBCFAs and their derived sphingolipids in the intestine are essential and sufficient for postembryonic development.
source_text: Previous studies on elo-5, acs-1, tat-2, and cgt-1/cgt-3 mutants suggested that biosynthesis and localization of mmBCFAs and their derived sphingolipids in the intestine are essential and sufficient for postembryonic development
